lesson: Identify only the three task bowls, keep IDs stable among distractors. Only current RGB and public robot calibration can guide actions.
Holding supported, positively empty and uncertain require different decisions. Do not conflate occlusion with loss; do not ignore positive loss evidence.
Relocation must be visually reviewed and currently localized before it becomes the stack base. Staging, destination and object dimensions are independent.
Inspect actual nesting after each release. Reacquire and regrasp the same bowl after a clear miss; uncertain alone is not a failure verdict.

A new empty relocation site is optional. Prefer nesting onto a currently supported task bowl with visually exposed rim and clear overhead access; a failed free-space proposal must not block all direct transfers.

Failed remeasurement does not block an existing placement plan: retain the previous held offset and confirmed destination. Fresh geometry improves an estimate when available; absence of a new fit is not a new prohibition.

Use bowl-centered local planning with its opening generally upward; no fixed gripper heading. Intermediate poses are soft targets, final nesting aligns the bowl center. Try Cartesian motion first, graph/trajectory search second. A numerical motion failure changes the local action without re-asking whether the unchanged held bowl is still held. Native budget is advisory until native termination.
